correctness.rationale: Taking as hypotheses the precise phase ODEs quoted from Kim, set M=m+n, alpha=a-pi/2, beta=b-pi/4. The Jacobian has eigenvalues M/sqrt(2)>0 and -1/sqrt(2)<0, so the backwards-time convergent nontrivial branch is the unique local unstable manifold beta=c alpha²+O(alpha³). Its invariance equation gives 2Mc=1/4-c and c=1/[4(2M+1)]. Then q=csc a=1+alpha²/2+O(alpha^4), r=tan b=1+alpha²/[2(2M+1)]+O(alpha³), hence lim(q-1)/(r-1)=2M+1. Since y=xr and q=dy/dx, x d(r-1)/dx=2M(r-1)+O((r-1)^{3/2}). The angular error is integrable along x down to zero, giving r-1=C x^{2M}(1+o(1)) with C>0 and contact order 2M+1. The source verify.py correctly expands the exact quoted ODE and invariance coefficient; independently checked the linear/quadratic terms. This establishes the local conditional conclusion for all integers m,n>=1; source classification supplies existence of the geometric end. Full publisher manuscript was inaccessible, so exact transcription of its starting vector field and identification of the correct geometric branch remain unverified primary-premise risks.
residual_risks: Source Kim full manuscript could not be inspected; initial phase coordinate field and origin-to-p4 branch taken from the audited source transcription, not independently checked against actual primary PDF.
Coefficient C>0 is dilation-dependent; the theorem gives no universal value for C and does not cover all other phase ends.
